text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: service=redwood-runtime region=us-west-2 metric=p99_latency threshold=2500ms value=3402ms — paging oncall
elaine_oncall: I'm on it. pinging SRE and runtime. any evidence this is multi-tenant vs model-specific?
chris_sre: seeing cluster-wide p95 jump too. host-level IO iowait up on several GPU hosts. attaching tail of iostat:
chris_sre: ```Device:         tps    kB_read/s    kB_wrtn/s    kB_read    kB_wrtn
nvme0n1        85.3       2048.1      41200.6   12345678   247890123
nvme1n1       160.7       5032.4     132001.8   30234567  792345678```
raj_runtime: also seeing streaming stalls: many sessions stuck in SEND state waiting on disk read for KV cache cold misses. KV hitrate dropped from 0.92 -> 0.55 around 02:12 UTC.
lena_ops: which tenants are spiking IO? I can correlate cgroup stats.
chris_sre: preliminary: tenant-tenor (customer id t-842) has heavy batch encoding jobs and a legacy worker that does large checkpoint writes to /var/tmp. top cgroup I/O:
chris_sre: ```cgroup: tenant-tenor (gid 230) read_kB/s=4200 write_kB/s=89000 iops=2200```
elaine_oncall: if that's true, we should throttle or evict that tenant from the shared pool now. Can someone run the eviction playbook?
raj_runtime: we can shift tenant-tenor to an isolated pool (dedicated-evict) or throttle via cgroup blkio.weight. Throttle will be quicker. Suggest: blkio.weight change from 500 -> 100 for that cgroup. Command: `echo 100 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant-230/blkio.weight`
lena_ops: I'll push a temporary cgroup change and follow up with an eviction if things don't improve. running now.
prod-obs-bot: obs: post-throttle p99 latency improved from 3402ms -> 980ms within 18s; p95 went from 620 -> 210ms.
elaine_oncall: nice, keep me posted. Raj please confirm no regressions from throttling (KV eviction churn, OOMs).
raj_runtime: monitoring KV size/residency — no immediate surge. However, streaming stall traces show some older model endpoints still using on-disk checkpoints (model-legacy-v1). If eviction persists, we might cause higher CPU contends for checkpoint load.
chris_sre: confirm: I see kernel writeback spikes dropping after throttle; CPU softirq still a bit high on a few hosts though.
elaine_oncall: good. Next steps: 1) keep throttle for 15 min 2) if stable, schedule live migration of tenant-tenor to dedicated-reserved pool 3) create follow-up to force customer to use dedicated for heavy batch jobs or add quota
lena_ops: throttle applied at 02:18 UTC. tracking host metrics and per-tenant IO. I'll start migration when we have a maintenance window or can live-migrate workloads.
raj_runtime: quick mitigation checklist ran: `kv-cache:prefetch=on`, `streaming-batch-size=auto`, `io-qos=tenant-230:100` — pushing to hosts now.
chris_sre: adding kernel-level niceness for the checkpoint writer: `chrt -f 10 /usr/local/bin/checkpoint-writer` to reduce scheduling interference. queued on affected hosts.
elaine_oncall: customer impact: observed increased generator latency and some streaming stalls for customers routed to us-west-2 between 02:10-02:20 UTC. No data-exfil or errors; only increased latency and a handful of aborted streaming sessions (~0.03% of sessions). Notify CS/Account team?
raj_runtime: yes, flagging to account team: tenant-tenor's batch job caused collateral impact. Recommend email: summary + remediation plan + suggested dedicated capacity.
prod-obs-bot: new metric: kv-cache hitrate recovering: 0.55 -> 0.85 after throttling and checkpoint backpressure.
elaine_oncall: OK looks stable for now. I'll start a short post-incident thread to scope follow-up: root cause, customer-impact timeline, runbook gaps. Assigning owners:
elaine_oncall: - remediation (lena_ops) - live migration + coord with infra
elaine_oncall: - runtime changes (raj_runtime) - make throttling auto when IO burst detected
elaine_oncall: - customer comms (chris_sre) - draft and handoff to CS
lena_ops: ack. I'll capture exact host IDs and cgroup paths, and prepare migration playbook.
raj_runtime: ack. I'll add auto QoS rule: if cluster p95 > 1500ms and per-host write_kB/s > 40MB/s, then apply per-tenant blkio.weight cap. Drafting PR for the operator.
chris_sre: will draft incident note and notify account manager for tenant-tenor.
elaine_oncall: handoff to eng-oncall for follow-up. tagging @eng-oncall for tomorrow's rotation. If anyone sees a re-escalation ping this thread. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
prod-obs-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. Final p99 observed after mitigation 860ms.
elaine_oncall: closing the active pager; leaving thread open for post-incident writeup and action items.
